order: a day off: just carry on tomorrow
safety: no guilt: a missed day never undoes the others
count real money with a grown-up

little.twist: Bobo's tower falls twice, and Pip-pop's sweets look yummy.
little.can_now: pick a goal they can do, build it one step at a time, try again after a fall and save for something bigger

steps.say: Bobo has a dream: a tower as tall as the window! A dream is something you wish for. Let's help Bobo make a plan.
A dream is big. A goal is one thing you can do. Which is a good goal for today?

choices.why: That's a big wish. A goal is something you can do and see, like 3 blocks high.
When? A goal says what, and when.

steps.done: 3 blocks high: a goal Bobo can do today!

steps.say: Big jobs go one step at a time. Help Bobo build: the big block, then the middle one, then the small one.
steps.done: Three blocks high!

steps.say: Oh! A wobble, and the tower fell down. That's OK: it happens to every builder.
What does Bobo do now?

choices.text: Try again, a bit more carefully

choices.why: Giving up means no tower. Falls help us learn: try again!
That won't help. Take a breath, then try again.

steps.done: Trying again: that's how builders do it.

steps.say: Build it again, slowly: big, middle, small.
steps.done: Three blocks high, and it stays up! Bobo kept going.

steps.say: Oh no, it fell again! Builders don't stop: they look at why. The big block was on a wobbly bit of the floor.
Once more, on the flat mat this time: big, middle, small.
steps.done: It stands! Two falls, and Bobo still did it.

steps.say: Bobo is saving for a kite. He has 2 coins. Pip-pop sells sweets for 2 coins. What gets Bobo his kite?

choices.text: Keep the coins in his saving jar

choices.why: Sweets are nice, but then the kite takes longer. Saving brings the big thing closer.

choices.text: Leave the coins on the floor
choices.why: Coins in a jar are safe: they're there when you need them.

steps.done: Saving now, for something better later.

steps.say: Pip-pop says: "Sweets are only 1 coin today!" Bobo still wants his kite. What does he do?

choices.text: Keep saving: the kite is what he really wants

choices.why: Cheap is still coins out of the jar. Bobo's goal is the kite.
That empties the jar. The kite needs his coins.

steps.done: Bobo waited: the kite gets closer.

steps.say: Help Bobo put his 2 coins in the saving jar: tap the jar 2 times.
steps.done: 2 coins saved for the kite.

steps.say: A habit is a small good thing you do every day. Bobo's habit: water his plant each morning.
Water the plant: hold the watering can over it.
steps.done: The plant drinks it up.

steps.label: 5 days
steps.say: The days go by. Bobo waters his plant every morning... except one day, when he forgets.
Bobo forgot one day. What now?

choices.text: Water it the next day: it waited for him

choices.why: One forgotten day is fine! Just carry on the next day.
No need! Everyone forgets sometimes. Tomorrow is a new day.

steps.done: The plant waited, and it grew again.

steps.say: You helped Bobo with a goal, steps, trying again, saving and a habit. Now make your own: open MY GOAL BOARD!

choices.text: something you can do and see

check.say: Your tower falls down. What do you do?
Saving coins in a jar helps you...
You forgot your habit one day. Then you...

name_it.title: One step at a time
lines: A goal is something you can do and see.
Big jobs: one step at a time.
If it falls down, try again.
Save now for something better later.
A small habit every day: a missed day is fine.
name_it.source: The Dunedin study of self-control (Moffitt et al., 2011) and research on how habits form (Lally et al., 2010)

little.try_real: With a grown-up: choose one small goal for this week, like a tower of 10 blocks or laying the table, and plan its first step.

sources.fact: Self-control in childhood predicts health, wealth and staying out of trouble as adults, and it can be learned.
sources.source: Moffitt et al. (2011), PNAS 108(7), the Dunedin study

sources.fact: A new daily habit took from 18 to 254 days to become automatic (66 in the middle); missing one day did not materially affect it.
sources.source: Lally, van Jaarsveld, Potts and Wardle (2010), European Journal of Social Psychology 40(6)

sources.fact: Waiting for something better and finishing what you start are self-mastery skills for young children.

middle.twist: Two things get in the way. Can your plan handle both?
middle.can_now: set a goal they can check, put its steps in order and make a 'When ..., I will ...' plan

steps.say: Your dream: fly your own rocket to the Moon! Dreams need a goal, steps and a plan. Let's put them on your Goal Board.
Which is a goal you can check?

choices.text: Save {moon_gold} gold for Mission Control's Moon rocket in 3 weeks

choices.why: Better how? A goal you can check says what, how much and by when.
That's the dream! The goal is the next big thing you can check.

steps.done: What, how much, by when: a goal you can check.

steps.say: Pin your goal on the board: touch the GOAL space.
steps.done: Your goal is on the board.

steps.say: What comes first? Touch the step cards in the right order.
steps.done: LEARN, SAVE, BUY, BUILD: one step at a time, the dream gets closer.

steps.say: Plans work best as 'When ..., I will ...'. Which plan is best?

choices.text: "When I finish a lesson, I put 10 gold aside for my rocket."

choices.why: When? A plan with a 'when' tells your brain the moment to do it.

choices.text: "I'll save it all at the end."
choices.why: Small amounts after each lesson add up, and they're easier.

steps.done: When... I will...: your brain knows the moment.

steps.say: Pin your plan on the board: touch the PLAN space.
steps.done: Your plan is on the board.

steps.say: What if a friend asks you to play just when you planned your lesson?

choices.why: Once often becomes always. Say 'after my lesson', and play then.
Play is good too! A plan finds time for both.

steps.done: An if-then plan for what gets in the way.

steps.say: And one evening you're very tired. If you're tired, then...

choices.text: ...I do just a tiny part: one question

choices.why: A tiny part keeps the plan going. Skipping a week makes it hard to start again.
Sleep matters. Do a tiny part, then rest.

steps.done: Two obstacles, two if-then plans. Your plan can handle both.

steps.say: Habits help goals. Pick one small habit for the practice garden:

choices.reply: Water: good for your body and your brain.
Reading: a little every day adds up to a lot.
Tidy: everything is easier to find.
Helping: everyone at home is glad.

steps.say: A week of your habit. Wednesday has a cloud: that's the day you forgot. Touch every day you kept it.
steps.done: Six days kept. The plant grew on every one of them.

steps.say: You forgot one day. Is the habit ruined?

choices.text: No: one day off hardly matters. Carry on.

choices.why: Scientists found one missed day hardly matters. Just carry on.
No need! Habits take weeks to stick, with a few days off.

steps.done: Right: carry on, and it sticks.

steps.say: Three lessons done this week. Keep your plan: tap the rocket jar after each one, 3 times.
steps.done: 30 gold aside for the rocket. The plan works!

steps.say: A goal you can check, steps in order, a when-then plan and a habit. Now make your real one: open MY GOAL BOARD!

check.say: Which is a goal you can check?

choices.text: "When I finish a lesson, I save 10 gold."

check.say: One missed day of a habit...
A friend asks you to play during your plan. You...

name_it.title: A goal you can reach
lines: A goal you can check: what, how much, by when.
A plan for what gets in the way.
Small habits: a missed day hardly matters.
name_it.source: Gollwitzer and Sheeran (2006), if-then plans; Lally et al. (2010), how habits form

middle.try_real: With a grown-up: set one small goal and plan its first step. Write your 'When ..., I will ...' plan on paper and stick it where you'll see it.

sources.fact: If-then plans ('when X happens, I will do Y') make reaching a goal much more likely, across many studies (d = 0.65).
sources.source: Gollwitzer and Sheeran (2006), Advances in Experimental Social Psychology 38

sources.fact: Missing one opportunity to do a new habit did not materially affect how the habit formed.
sources.source: Lally et al. (2010), European Journal of Social Psychology

sources.fact: Goals in steps and a small daily habit are self-mastery skills for 9 to 11 year olds.
sources.source: EntreComp (2016): planning and management, motivation and perseverance

big.twist: A second obstacle gets in the way, and the goal check is trickier.
big.can_now: plan a goal with WOOP and if-then plans, put big things first and bounce back with an honest look at progress

steps.say: Big goals need plans that work on busy days. Let's build yours from parts, the way scientists suggest.
Which goal is clear, can be measured, and has a date?

choices.text: Earn 3 By myself stamps in Life by the end of the month

choices.why: Too big to check. Pick one thing, a number and a date.
Which stuff, and how will you know? Pick one thing, a number and a date.

steps.done: One thing, a number, a date: you'll know when you've done it.

steps.say: Which goal is clear, can be measured, and has a date?

choices.text: Master lots of School lessons soon
choices.why: 'Lots' and 'soon' can't be checked. Say how many, and by when.
Too much to be real. A clear goal is a stretch you can reach.

steps.done: 2 lessons by Friday: clear, measurable, dated.

steps.say: Scientists found a strong order for a plan: the WISH, the best OUTCOME, the OBSTACLE inside you, then the PLAN. Touch them in order.
steps.done: Wish, Outcome, Obstacle, Plan: WOOP!

steps.say: Your if-then plan. First the WHEN: pick a moment you'll notice.

choices.why: Feelings come and go. Pick a moment that happens every day.
'Sometime' never comes. Pick a real moment.

steps.done: A real moment your brain can watch for.

steps.say: Now the THEN: a small, clear action.

choices.text: I practise one Life skill for 10 minutes

choices.why: Hard how? Say exactly what you'll do.
Too big. Small and clear is easier to start.

steps.done: "When I finish dinner, I practise one Life skill for 10 minutes."

steps.say: Your obstacle: you're often tired after dinner. Your if-then:

choices.text: If I'm tired, then I do just 5 minutes
If I'm tired, then I skip the whole week
choices.why: A tiny part keeps the plan alive. Skipping makes it hard to start again.
Planning for the obstacle is the secret: it will happen sometimes.

steps.done: A plan for the obstacle: the strongest part of WOOP.

steps.say: A second obstacle: you want to play a game instead. Your if-then:

choices.text: If I want to play, then I play after my 10 minutes
If I want to play, then I play all evening
choices.why: Then the plan never happens. Play after: you get both.
Too strict to keep. Play after your 10 minutes.

steps.done: Two obstacles, two plans.

steps.say: Your week is a jar. Put in the big rocks first (the important things), then the pebbles, then the sand.
steps.done: Big things first: then the small ones fit round them.

steps.say: You missed your goal by one stamp. What helps most?

choices.text: Look at what went wrong, change the plan, try again

choices.why: Skills grow with practice: you're not bad at it, you're learning.
Blaming doesn't change the plan. Look at what you can change.

steps.done: Bouncing back: learn from it, change the plan, go again.

steps.say: Habits stick when you tie them to something you already do. Which plan?

choices.text: "After I brush my teeth, I read one page."

choices.why: Remembering is the hard part: tie it to something you already do.
Small and often sticks better than big and rare.

steps.done: Tied to brushing your teeth: it happens every day.

steps.label: 30 days
steps.say: A month with your plan goes by...
At the end of the month you have 2 stamps, not 3. What goes on your Goal Board?

choices.why: Honest numbers help you plan better. 2 of 3 is real progress.
2 of 3 is good progress. Keep the board, change the plan.

steps.done: Honest progress: the best way to plan the next step.

steps.say: A clear goal, WOOP, if-then plans, big things first and honest progress. Open MY GOAL BOARD and build your real one!

choices.text: a moment you'll notice, and a small clear action
a feeling and a big promise
the important things first, then the small ones round them

check.say: You missed your goal. What helps most?

choices.text: change the plan and try again

check.say: Your progress is 2 of 3. You write...

name_it.title: Plans that stick
lines: If-then plans: for the moment, and for the obstacle.
Missed it? Change the plan and try again.
name_it.source: Mental contrasting with implementation intentions (Oettingen and Gollwitzer: WOOP) and Gollwitzer and Sheeran (2006)

big.try_real: With a grown-up: do a WOOP for a real goal (a sport, a subject, a skill), with one if-then plan for your biggest obstacle.

sources.fact: Fifth graders taught mental contrasting with implementation intentions (WOOP-style plans) improved their grades, attendance and conduct.
sources.source: Duckworth, Kirby, Gollwitzer and Oettingen (2013), Social Psychological and Personality Science

sources.fact: If-then plans make reaching goals much more likely (d = 0.65).
Resilience, motivation and self-awareness are among the skills employers rank highest.
